facts.claim: 作者主张把烂笑话统称 dad jokes 对父亲不太公平，这是全章立论的起点
facts.quote: Rubbish jokes are often referred to as ‘dad jokes’, which seems slightly unfair on fathers.

facts.claim: 他用 dad jeans、dad bods、dad rock 作旁证，说明 dad 已被当成“糟糕”的同义词用在各个领域
facts.quote: with dad jeans, dad bods and dad rock all failing to impress anyone.

facts.claim: 第一条解释是喜剧变精致后需要差异化：可复述的小段子失去了“joke”这个旧名，得另起一个名字
facts.quote: Now, the bite-sized bit of repeatable comedy that used to just be called a ‘joke’ needs its own name.

facts.claim: 他举例说旧式父亲回家只跟孩子正式握手、道晚安，然后自己去喝一码威士忌
facts.quote: Dads of the past came home from work, gave their children a formal handshake, bade them goodnight and relaxed with a yard of whisky.

facts.claim: 第二条解释是历史遗留：过去的父亲与孩子相处极少，用顺手就来的肉麻笑话弥补彼此不熟
facts.quote: there’s massive relationship-building value in reeling off some zingers.

facts.claim: 第三条解释是父亲地位下降：二十世纪后半叶大众媒体兴起、女性大量进入职场，笨拙的情景喜剧爸爸成了新刻板印象
facts.quote: the advent of mass media as well as the huge influx of women into the workforce brought dads down a peg or two

facts.claim: 他承认妈妈同样可以无聊透顶，但“dad”更适合当“过时又不靠谱”的前缀，并说爸爸确实特别爱讲这类笑话
facts.quote: While mums are just as capable of being tediously, obnoxiously unfunny as dads are, dads do seem particularly enthusiastic about bad jokes

facts.claim: 他用蘑菇笑话当例证：爸爸看见蘑菇就要讲“吃太多没蘑菇（没空）”并自称 fun guy，被嫌弃还继续
facts.quote: unable to see a mushroom without pointing out that they’ve eaten so much they don’t have mushroom for anything else

relations.pair: dad jeans / dad bods / dad rock
relations.relation: 三者与 dad jokes 并列，共同证明 dad 已从亲属称谓变成“不入流”的形容词，为“为什么叫爸爸笑话”提供语言环境
relations.quote: with dad jeans, dad bods and dad rock all failing to impress anyone.

relations.pair: 精致单口喜剧 / 可复述小段子
relations.relation: 作者把两者对立：前者有 introspection, depth and truth 但带不走，后者能被记住并转述，所以需要独立命名
relations.quote: If you watch a critically beloved, intricately crafted comedy set laden with introspection, depth and truth

relations.pair: ‘Hi Hungry, I’m Dad!’ / 蘑菇笑话
relations.relation: 两条都是自动播放式的字面误解（把 Hungry 当名字、把 mushroom 拆成 mush room），作者用它们说明爸爸笑话的固定套路
relations.quote: ‘Dad, I’m hungry!’ / ‘Hi Hungry, I’m Dad!’ remains.

relations.relation: 作者明确比较两个称谓，认为把“过时、不靠谱”安在爸爸头上比安在妈妈头上更说得通
relations.quote: ‘dad’ makes a lot more sense than ‘mum’.

numbers.value: the second half of the 20th century
numbers.meaning: 大众媒体兴起与女性大量进入职场的时段，作者用它标记“笨爸爸”刻板印象的形成期
numbers.quote: In the second half of the 20th century, the advent of mass media as well as the huge influx of women into the workforce

numbers.meaning: 父亲的家庭地位被拉低了“一两级”，是作者对地位下降幅度的量化说法
numbers.quote: brought dads down a peg or two
